title: Sorting press: Proof strip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Merge sort. Return the whole result list in the order you built it.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
readings is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless Step 1 says otherwise. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
Sort readings from smallest to largest using merge sort. To use merge sort, split the list into smaller parts, sort those parts, then join the sorted parts in order. Keep all repeated numbers. The result list is the sorted list.

Step 2: Return the answer
Return the whole result list in the order you built it. If it is empty, return [].

Write your function
Complete sortingPressProofStrip(readings, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.
unitIntro: Sort readings from smallest to largest using merge sort. To use merge sort, split the list into smaller parts, sort those parts, then join the sorted parts in order. Keep all repeated numbers. The result list is the sorted list. Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n log n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.

referenceSolutions.python:
def sortingPressProofStrip(readings, k):
    a=readings
    out=[]
    def sort(xs):
        if len(xs)<2: return xs
        mid=len(xs)//2
        left,right=sort(xs[:mid]),sort(xs[mid:])
        merged=[]
        i=j=0
        while i<len(left) or j<len(right):
            if j==len(right) or (i<len(left) and left[i]<=right[j]):
                merged.append(left[i])
                i+=1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                j+=1
        return merged
    out=sort(a[:])
    return out
